Thirty-four comments

Here is The Laurel Tree, as requested by Squeezebox. This version comes from Henrik Norbeck’s collection. I should say that it is slightly different from the version I have - bar 4 of the 1st and 2nd parts can be played: BAGB A (3Bcd .

I have also heard a couple of diffferent versions of the 2nd part:

|: eaag egdc|BAGA Bcdg|eaag egdc|BAGA A2 (3Bcd|
eaag egdc|BAGA Bcd2|~e3f gaaf|gedB A2 (3Bcd :||

i.e. bars 1 to 8 of the second part are repeated instead of playing bars 9 to 16.

and:

|:eaag egdc|BAGA Bcdg|eaag a2ga|bagb ~a3g|
eaag egdc|BAGA Bcd2|~e3f gaaf|gedB A2 (3Bcd :||

i.e. bars 9 to 16 of the second part are repeated instead of playing bars 1 to 8.

It’s very hard to explain what I’m on about without playing it. I hope the abcs make it clear.

The version played by Brian Finnegan (with hair) as the second tune in this set:

It is a rocking, brilliant tune, though you have to have some skill with flutter tonguing to be able to play it. Brian is playing what I think is a G Patrick Olwell bamboo flute in the video. This is a transcription of Matt Molloy’s version of the Laurel Tree taken from what I assume is a televised performance with the bothy band in 1977.

The performance can be found here for now https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6dzJ_qC2tHE&t=89

Re: The Laurel Tree

I’ve always wondered if this tune is named for the pub The Laurel Tree in Camden Town. Can anyone put me straight?

It could just refer to the tree (I note it’s sometimes called the Laurel Bush instead). But in the 1950s the Laurel Tree pub was one of the early venues for sessions in London, with Willie Clancy, Bobby Casey and Martin Byrnes among others playing there. (See Reg Hall’s interview with Tommy Healy (https://sounds.bl.uk/World-and-traditional-music/Reg-Hall-Archive/025M-C0903X0377XX-0100V0).

The tune itself is clearly older than the 1950s - a version was recorded by Tom Morrison in America in 1928 - but I haven’t so far found an earlier use of the Laurel Tree name. Tom Morrison called it the Castlebar Traveller.

The pub building still stands (at 113 Bayham Street) but is now a Brewdog.

Re: The Laurel Tree

Thanks for posting this jmeme version of this tune I’ve been playing for a long time.
Reading the comments, I also discovered its kinship with “Scatter the Mud”, thanks also to Slainte, much belatedly.
So I tried to put them together, and I think the result is really nice.
I went looking for a tune/slow tune to go with it, to make a “suite”.
The first piece that came to mind was this Breton qwerz, why? “Marev eo ma mestrez”.
This isn’t the subject of thesession so I’m not going to suggest this tune. I’ve rewritten it in ABC, but here it is:
X: 1
T: Marev eo ma mestrez
T: Traditional Breton
R: gwerz
L: 1/4
K: Amin
c>Bc | A2 G |(A3 |!fermata!A3)||
Acd | e>d e | c2 B|!fermata!A3 d|||
d3 | Bcd| e3 | ABc |B2 A | G (E2|!fermata!E2) e|
e3|cde| f>ed|e z A|A (G2|!fermata!G2) e|
e3|cde| f>ed|c2 B |(A3 |!fermata!A3) ||

(!fermata!) can be removed, but not all abc programs accept it.

(Deepl from french)

Instead of playing the Part B twice the same way, I have introduced the difference between first playing / repeat playing which is found in a lot of versions.
